fit: oral isolated piperine and two spatial memory outcomes in an AF64A rat model
assessment: Original Results 3.1 and Figs. 1–2 report improved escape latency and retention across piperine doses against the injury vehicle group (p<.001). The preparation, species, experimental injury and spatial tasks leave culinary pepper and sustained attention in Parkinson disease unresolved.

fit: injected isolated piperine with distinct dose and timing contrasts in an STZ rat radial-arm task
assessment: At 2.5 mg/kg after injury, the original report shows 1.66 versus 5.66 mean reference errors (p<.05). Higher post-treatment doses did not significantly alter those errors, and selected comparisons favored other arms against the 5 mg/kg pretreatment group. The rat memory findings leave the frozen exposure and attention outcome open.

fit: oral leaf infusion in laboratory sleep tests with a separate injected citral comparison
assessment: The complete Part I body reports no tea potentiation of pentobarbital-induced sleep and no change in rat slow-wave or REM EEG measures. Injected isolated citral was the positive sleep-potentiation comparison. The digitized EEG dose labels disagree. The study provides no observation of enacted dreams or Parkinson-specific outcome.
